$comment: This file lives in the fiber-v0.1 bundle directory and describes fiber-query/0.2. The directory names the bundle of schemas shipped alongside the reference fixture set, not a version they all share: fiber-world/0.1 and fiber-context-certificate/0.1 have not moved, and renaming the directory would claim they had. No document declares the bundle name and nothing hashes it.
description: fiber-query/0.2 differs from 0.1 in exactly one way: a reader refuses a document carrying a key declared nowhere here, rather than dropping it. No field was added, removed or retyped. This file already declared `additionalProperties: false` at 0.1 — the shipped readers were not enforcing it, and 0.2 is that enforcement, so no document that was ever valid under this schema is invalidated. `goal` is newly listed: the compiler has always read it and this schema omitted it, which is the same drift `bioprism-governance` found and repaired on the certificate.

goal.description: The decision the section is assembled for, echoed verbatim into the Decision Section. Absent, the compiler substitutes its reference goal string so that sections stay byte-comparable with the CPython reference, which hard-codes one. The reference does not read this key; a query that supplies it compiles to different bytes in the two implementations, which is a defect in the reference recorded at `bioprism_fiber::REFERENCE_GOAL` and older than this version.

policy.description: Policy clauses the caller accepts as obligations, and therefore the grants this compile holds. Must be a subset of the clause list the world's `data_policy` fact declares, where the world declares one; a clause outside it is a policy conflict and the compile refuses. Facts whose `policy` scope names a clause absent from this list are withheld.

role.description: Caller role. Carried by the contract and read by no compiler pass; role and visibility filtering is not implemented.

schema_version.description: Both labels are read. 0.2 changed only what a reader does with an undeclared key, so a 0.1 document whose keys are all declared here is byte-for-byte a valid 0.2 document. Re-labelling one would move its `query_sha256` and therefore the digest of every certificate compiled from it — including the frozen reference pair three implementations agree on.

title: AURORA FIBER Query
